newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks discover more Holocaust accounts.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks discover more Holocaust accounts.

text.p: A Swiss banking ombudsman in charge of searching for dormant accounts of Holocaust victims said on Tuesday banks had discovered an extra 1.6 million Swiss francs ($1.3 million) in unclaimed wealth.

Ombudsman Hanspeter Haeni said his search had come across 11 valid claims out of nearly 900 detailed inquiries. Three of the 11 were held in the name of bank customers murdered by the Nazis, he said in a statement.

"Two other customers were Jews who lived in Romania and were totally dispossessed during the war on account of discriminatory legislation," Haeni said in a text prepared for delivery to a news conference. He did not name them or the banks involved.
"Switzerland will and indeed must continue to maintain access to dormant accounts via the banking ombudsman," he said.

Haeni, whose work has been dismissed by Jewish critics as a "cruel hoax" designed to protect Swiss banks, said his office would continue to act as the central contact point for Holocaust account inquiries for an indefinite period.

He said up to 20 detailed inquiries in the form of questionnaires were coming in every day and that he would make another public appearance in the summer of 1997 to give an update on the status of the search.
